picked.body: 베트남 호치민시의 한 재래시장. 베트남에서 4%대 고물가가 이어지고 있는 것으로 나타났다. 베트남 재무부 통계국(NSO)이 지난 3일 내놓은 ‘2026년 8월 사회경제적 현황’ 보고서에 따르면, 8월 베트남의 소비자물가지수(CPI)는 전월 대비 0.47%, 전년 동월 대비 4.89% 오른 것으로 잠정 집계됐다. 올 들어 8월 기준 평균 CPI는 전년 동기 대비 4.45% 상승률을 나타냈다. 에너지·의료비·교육비 등 국가가 관리하는 품목과 가격변동성이 높은 식품을 제외한 근원 CPI는 4.24% 상승했다. 지난 8월 CPI는 전월과 비교해 전체 구성요소 11개 상품·서비스군 가운데 식품·외식을 제외한 10개 항목이 일제히 상승했다. 이 중 교통·운송비는 4.09% 올라 CPI를 0.41%포인트 끌어올리는 등 물가 상승의 주범으로 꼽혔다. 이는 다른 소비재·서비스 품목군에 비해 훨씬 큰 상승폭이다. 반면, 식품·외식 부문은 0.03% 내려 전체 CPI를 0.01%포인트 낮췄다. 이 중 식료품 가격지수는 0.05% 내려 CPI를 0.01%포인트 낮췄고, 곡물 가격은 0.04% 하락했다. 반대로 외식 부문은 0.01% 올랐지만 전체 CPI에는 거의 영향을 주지 않았다. 다른 품목군을 보면 8월 주류·담배는 전월 대비 0.12% 올랐는데, 주로 소비 수요 증가와 원자재 생산비용 상승이 겹친 영향으로 풀이됐다. 의류·모자·신발 부문은 전월 대비 0.11% 올랐는데, 주로 신학기를 앞둔 구매 수요 증가에 기인했다. 주택, 전기·수도, 연료 및 건축자재는 0.1% 상승했고, 가전·가정용품 부문은 0.19% 올랐는데, 주로 원·부자재비와 인건비 상승 영향으로 풀이됐다. 의약품·의료서비스 부문은 전월 대비 0.05% 올랐는데, 주로 원자재비 상승에 따라 일부 의약품 가격이 소폭 오른 영향이다. 정보·통신 부문은 0.08% 올랐다. 특히 8월 교육비는 0.47% 올랐다. 이 중 교육 서비스 가격은 0.57% 올랐는데, 일부 지역의 사립대학·중고등학교, 사립 유치원들이 2026~2027학년도 학비를 인상한 영향으로 풀이됐다. 이 외 종이제품은 0.37%, 필기구류는 0.34%, 문구류·기타 학용품 가격은 0.29% 올랐다. 문화·오락·관광 부문은 0.03% 올랐는데, 세부 가격지수에서는 주로 도서·신문·잡지류 가격(+0.27%), 국내여행(+0.2%), 스포츠용품(+0.19%), 장난감(+0.15%), 호텔(+0.06%) 등에 상승에 집중됐다. 반대로 해외여행 가격은 0.24% 내렸고, 영화·공연 관람은 1.02%, 스포츠시설 이용권은 0.09% 하락했다. 기타 상품·서비스 부문은 전월 대비 0.15% 올랐다.

picked.t: Samsung Vietnam reports $2.3B profit in H1
picked.body: Samsung Thai Nguyen, Samsung Electronics Vietnam (Bac Ninh), Samsung Display Vietnam (Bac Ninh), and Samsung Electronics HCMC CE Complex posted combined revenues of $35.2 billion in the period, up 21%, according to Samsung's latest financial report. Samsung Thai Nguyen, which manufactures mobile phones and telecommunications equipment, reported the highest revenues and profits, $16.2 billion and $1.08 billion, among the four units. The figures represented increases of 22.4% and 33.4%. Another phone factory, Samsung Electronics Vietnam, was second in terms of revenues, at $9.1 billion, while its profits topped $670 million. Roh Tae Moon, CEO of Samsung Electronics, said these two phone factories in the northern region, after 17 years in Vietnam, achieved cumulative exports of US$500 billion as of the end of June. Samsung Display Vietnam also reported increases in revenues and profits. Samsung Electronics HCMC CE Complex was the only one of the four to report a decline in profits, which fell from $180 million to $160 million. Samsung is South Korea's largest privately owned conglomerate, with core businesses spanning electronics, finance, heavy industry and technology. Starting with a television manufacturing plant in HCMC in 1995, it has become Vietnam's largest foreign-owned business with investments exceeding $24 billion as of the end of 2025. Globally, Samsung reported sales of $206 billion and profits of $80 billion for the first half of 2026, representing increases of two and nine times from the same period last year. China was its largest market, generating $59.7 billion in revenues and surpassing the U.S. and the Americas, which reported sales of $47.6 billion. Analysts say Samsung's surge in profits has been driven by storage and memory chips as artificial intelligence applications, particularly AI agents, expand into tasks requiring greater computing capacity.

picked.t: Hanoi launches real-time flood map with instant alerts
picked.body: All data is extracted directly from an automatic monitoring station system managed and operated by Hanoi Sewerage and Drainage Company Limited. Rainfall conditions and floodwater depths are updated continuously in real time, with rainfall measured to the millimeter and water depth to the meter. The map uses a standard color scale to provide a visual assessment, enabling residents to gauge the level of danger within seconds. The application is expected to strengthen the capital's disaster response capacity while helping residents plan safer routes during the rainy and stormy season. The mini app is embedded directly into iHanoi, which already has 6.484 million registered accounts. This "all-in-one" model enables users to access potentially life-saving information immediately without having to install a separate application, saving device storage space and reducing access time on both Android and iOS devices. The application can also proactively send alerts directly to users' phones, meaning they can receive notifications without opening the app. When flooding or heavy rainfall occurs within a user's designated area, the system automatically displays a detailed pop-up alert, enabling residents to change their routes proactively. Users can set an alert radius ranging from 1km to 100km from their current location. They can also set specific hours for receiving notifications to avoid being disturbed outside their normal daily routines or at night. The map helps users avoid accidents caused by submerged manholes, potholes and fast-flowing water, while minimizing vehicle repair costs resulting from engine failure and damage to property. Location and notification permissions are clearly displayed, allowing users to choose whether to grant access. Even without granting location access, the mini app can still be used in basic map-search mode. The map is designed to serve millions of residents, drivers and visitors across the capital. Office workers and students, for example, can select routes that avoid flooded areas before leaving home. Ride-hailing drivers, delivery workers and truck drivers can protect their vehicles and cargo while avoiding breakdowns caused by floodwater. Households in low-lying areas can use the information to move belongings and vehicles to safer locations in anticipation of heavy rain. Transport and logistics businesses can adjust their routes based on real-time conditions, while disaster response agencies can gain an overall picture of the situation and respond more quickly. Residents can start using the service in three simple steps: download and open the iHanoi app; grant location and notification permissions to receive alerts relevant to their area; and set an appropriate alert radius and notification schedule to suit their daily routines. The launch of the map on iHanoi marks a new step forward in smart urban governance and disaster prevention in the capital. The deployment of advanced technology, combined with proactive action by the authorities, has the potential to change the way millions of residents respond to natural disasters.

picked.t: Vietnam nominates 5 candidates for World's Best Tourism Village
picked.body: The National Tourism Administration announced that five destinations have been put forward for UN Tourism’s annual "Best Tourism Villages" award. They are Lo (Dak Lak Province), Cat Cat Community Tourism Village (Lao Cai Province), Bay Mau Cam Thanh Nipa Palm Forest (Da Nang), Mang Den Treehouse Village (Quang Ngai Province), and Huu Lien Community Tourism Village (Lang Son Province). Cat Cat Community Tourism Village (Lao Cai Province) Cat Cat village is three kilometers from Sa Pa on the road to Fansipan. Home to the Mong ethnic minority, the village dates back to the mid-19th century. Since then, it has grown into a community tourism site. Cat Cat attracts visitors who are keen to explore the culture of Vietnam's northwestern highlands. A stone path winds down the mountainside past terraced rice fields and wooden houses. Streams, water wheels, wooden bridges, and Tien Sa Waterfall form the landscape. The Mong people grow rice and practice traditional crafts like linen weaving and silver carving. Photo courtesy of Cat Cat Village Visitors can take part in festivals, learn about Mong customs, sample specialties like corn wine and thang co stew, made from the meat and offal of horses or buffaloes, and check out handicrafts. Photo courtesy of Facebook/Ban Cat Cat Huu Lien Community Tourism Village (Lang Son Province) Huu Lien sits within the Huu Lien Nature Reserve in the core zone of the Lang Son UNESCO Global Geopark. It is known for its biodiversity, with protected forests, caves, limestone mountains, and waterfalls. The village has 40 homestays and guesthouses, built in the style of stilt houses but offering most modern comforts. Photo courtesy of Lang Son Newspaper Visitors to Huu Lien can kayak on Nong Dung Lake or camp at the Michi Camp ecological site. A highlight is Dong Lam Grassland, whose look shifts with the seasons. During the rainy season, from July to October, the plain floods over and looks both dramatic and dreamlike. Photo by Hung Vi Bay Mau Cam Thanh Nipa Palm Forest (Da Nang) The Bay Mau nipa palm forest lies three kilometers from Hoi An ancient town and is bordered by the De Vong, Thu Bon, and Hoai rivers. Its brackish waters make it ideal for water coconut palms to grow. During wartime, the forest served as a revolutionary base. Today, it has become an ecotourism destination. Photo by VnExpress/Giang Huy Visitors come to Cam Thanh for basket-boat rides, an activity started in 2009 that grew popular after 2012, with basket-boat spinning performances being a main highlight. In some areas, boatmen demonstrate their spinning technique upon request, something that foreign tourists lap up. Photo by VnExpress/Giang Huy Mang Den Treehouse (Quang Ngai Province) Located near Dak Ke Lake in Mang Den Commune, the Mang Den Treehouse site was recognized as a tourist destination in August 2025. Visitors are encouraged to spend their time meditating, reading, or listening to the sounds of the forest. Photo courtesy of Mang Den Treehouse Its houses, built on tree trunks or wooden stilts amid the forest, give the site its sense of closeness to nature while respecting the ecosystem. Each features a balcony overlooking the valley or mountains. Photo courtesy of Mang Den Treehouse The place offers activities such as ziplining, cycling, and meditation, ideal for visitors seeking a retreat but with scenery to explore. Photo courtesy of Mang Den Treehouse Lo Village (Dak Lak Province) Lo Village, in Hoa Hiep Ward, spans more than 182 hectares and is home to around 10,600 people. Its name comes from the kilns once used to smoke and dry seafood, a trade that flourished decades ago. The village now has 1,500 households along the province's southern coastline, divided into three areas, with Lo 3 chosen as the site for the nomination. Lo is notable for its tiled-roof houses set among coconut trees leading straight to the sea, fishing trade, and festivals. Tourism began before 2021 as visitors sought out the fishing village's atmosphere and scenery. The village now has 72 accommodation facilities with 459 rooms. The annual Best Tourism Villages award recognizes places that balance tourism with cultural preservation, environmental protection, community support, and sustainability. Vietnam has previously won the award five times through Lo Lo Chai Village (Tuyen Quang Province), Quynh Son Cultural Village (Lang Son Province), Thai Hai Ethnic Village (Thai Nguyen Province), Tan Hoa Village (Quang Tri Province), and Tra Que Vegetable Village (Da Nang City). picked.t: Japanese man flies to Vietnam every month to pursue love
picked.body: In early 2022, Pham Thi Thanh An, the owner of a ramen restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City, was falsely accused during a dispute within the Japanese expatriate community. Refusing to back down, she presented evidence to clear her name, successfully defended her reputation, and secured a formal apology from her accuser. Watching the ordeal unfold from Japan, 34-year-old Hiroshi found himself quietly admiring the resilient woman. Two years later, Hiroshi quit his banking career and chose Vietnam for his first-ever trip abroad. He stopped by An’s ramen shop but was unable to meet her. Later, he sent her a message saying: "The noodles were delicious. When I return to Vietnam in June 2025, I will visit your restaurant again." She replied politely. True to his word, eight months later he messaged to say he was heading to Ho Chi Minh City and asked her for the address of her newly relocated eatery. On June 26, the two met for the first time. During his three days in town, he dropped by the restaurant every day, and An welcomed him with the warm hospitality she showed any visitor from abroad. Before he departed, she gave him a decorative traditional conical leaf hat from the restaurant's wall as a farewell keepsake. Hiroshi put it on and unexpectedly broke into tears, saying he had never met anyone who made him feel so welcome. Back in Japan, Hiroshi set out to win An over, booking monthly round-trip flights to Ho Chi Minh City solely to see her. But, daunted by the geographic distance and cultural divide, she kept her guard up and gave him no encouragement. When Hiroshi announced a mid-July visit, she lied and told him the restaurant was closed to avoid him. Undeterred, he rescheduled his flight for the end of the month, followed by return trips in August and September. In September 2025, upon learning he had landed at Tan Son Nhat International Airport, An gave her staff the day off and shuttered the restaurant. That afternoon, she sent him a firm text that said: "I value you as a friend, and I do not want to jeopardize our good relationship. Please stop pursuing me." Upon receiving the message, he turned around and immediately boarded a flight back to Japan. He stayed away throughout October, leading her to believe she had finally shaken off her persistent suitor. But he continued to quietly keep up with her social media. Seeing that she remained single, he held on to hope. In November and December 2025, he was back in Ho Chi Minh City. He spent his days sitting at her ramen restaurant and his evenings at her cocktail bar. She continued to keep her distance, leaving her staff to attend to him. His unwavering devotion eventually won over the employees, who began feeling sympathy for the Japanese man and urged their boss to reconsider. Taking a closer look during one of his visits, An noticed Hiroshi had lost a significant amount of weight from six months earlier. When she asked him, he replied: "Because you once mentioned that I would look better if I lost some weight." An was stunned that he had taken an offhand remark to heart. During that same conversation, she learned that, several months earlier, he had already booked tickets for until February 2026 and had recently booked for the four months following that. "I asked myself whether I would ever find another person in this lifetime with such genuine devotion," An says. She started to have feelings for him. When he returned in January 2026, she took the initiative and guided him around the city. He confessed then that his previous excuses that he was drawn by "the food and people of Ho Chi Minh City" and had "a passion for flying" had been a facade. "If I had told you right away that I was flying over every month because I was in love with you, I was afraid it would overwhelm you. I preferred being around you as a friend rather than coming on too strong and pushing you away forever." The lifelong bachelor had also began to experience some unexpected changes: A chronic insomnia that had plagued him since the age of 14 simply vanished every time he visited Vietnam and met An, and he managed to sleep deeply. In March 2026, he invited her to the resort island of Phu Quoc. Under a backdrop of fireworks, he presented her with a diamond ring and a bouquet of 209 roses and proposed to her. That evening, she asked him: "What if I had said no?" He said he would have still given her the ring as a keepsake and simply bought another one for his next proposal. "I was determined to marry you." The couple celebrated their wedding in July 2026. Standing before hundreds of guests, he trembled so much that he could barely keep his vows steady in his hands. Tears streamed down his face as he recalled the day he met the woman who transformed his world. "Since June 26, 2025, my life has completely changed. picked.t: Vietnam welcomes nearly 16 million foreign tourists in 8 months
picked.body: The number of international visitors in the first eight months of this year increased 14.4% from the same period in 2025 and equivalent to 63.6% of the full-year target. The August figure is notable as the month is usually considered part of the low season for international tourism. The result shows that the country's tourism market continued to maintain and expand its appeal. Air travel remained the main mode of entry, accounting for 83% of international arrivals, while arrivals by road continued to increase, particularly from neighboring countries. By region, Asia was still Vietnam's largest source market, with about 11.8 million visitors in the eight-month period, making up nearly 74% of the total and increasing 7.4% year-on-year. Europe recorded the strongest growth among major regions, at 53.4%, with about 2.68 million visitors. Arrivals from the Americas reached around 887,000, up 20.7%, while those from Oceania rose 23.3% to nearly 489,000. Africa sent about 45,000 visitors to Vietnam, up 25.1%. The tourism authority said the figures show that Vietnam is expanding its reach beyond nearby Asian markets, with strong growth from long-haul markets, helping diversify the visitor base and reduce dependence on individual markets. By country, China remained Vietnam's largest source market, with 3.54 million visitors, accounting for about 22.3% of the total. South Korea ranked second with approximately 2.76 million visitors, or 17.3%. Together, the two markets provided more than 6.3 million visitors, nearly 40% of the country's total. Russia ranked third with more than 1 million visitors, representing a year-on-year increase of about 165.7%, the highest growth among major source markets. Other key markets also posted strong growth. Visitors from the U.S. increased 20.4%, Cambodia 41.5%, Japan 9.2%, the Philippines 58.8% and Australia 23.3%. European markets continued to perform well, with arrivals from the U.K. rising 9.8%, France 13.4%, Germany 15.1%, Sweden 25.1%, Switzerland 27%, Poland 51.2% and the Czech Republic 28.2%. In Southeast Asia, tourists from Malaysia grew 20.5%, Singapore 31.7%, and Indonesia 26.7%. India was another fast-growing market. The number of Indian visitors rose from just 102,000 in 2019 to more than 612,000 in the first eight months of 2026. The expansion of direct air services between major Indian cities and Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, and Da Nang has helped make Vietnam more accessible to Indian travelers. The Russian market has also rebounded strongly, supported by Vietnam's growing appeal as a safe and attractive Asian destination and the resumption and expansion of charter flights connecting major Russian cities with Vietnamese beach destinations. The tourism authority said the results demonstrate positive growth in both visitor numbers and market diversity. With nearly 16 million international arrivals in eight months and the peak year-end travel season ahead, Vietnam is well placed to move closer to its yearly target of 25 million international visitors.

picked.t: Teacher spends nearly 10 years teaching Khmer in Vietnam's borderlands
picked.body: On a morning in early August, after more than two months of summer training, Ca Di watered the small garden in front of her house in Phuoc Vinh Commune. Her husband was on security duty at a school, so she sat with their eldest son, a second grader, reviewing lessons before the new school year. The youngest of four siblings, Ca Di grew up in a family of teachers. Her father and older sister were both teachers, and she developed an interest in teaching from an early age. While studying Khmer Literature Pedagogy at Tra Vinh University, she often watched reports about volunteer teachers working in remote areas and told herself she would one day do the same. In 2016, after graduating, she learned that Tan Bien District in Tay Ninh Province that borders Cambodia was recruiting primary school Khmer teachers. She took a bus more than 300 kilometers to submit her application. "I just thought I’d try. If it didn’t work out, at least it would be an experience," she recalls. Three months after taking the exam, she received her assignment to Hoa Dong Primary School. Her first days in the border region felt completely foreign, apart from the familiar curved roofs of Khmer temples among the sugar palm trees. With no relatives nearby and no guesthouses in the area, she became discouraged until a kindergarten teacher who had applied in the same recruitment round offered her a place to stay temporarily. Three months later, the school arranged accommodation in the teachers’ quarters. Once she had a place to live, another unexpected challenge emerged: the local dialect. Although both communities spoke Khmer, the dialects used in her hometown Tra Vinh and Tay Ninh differed enough to make early conversations difficult. "At first they couldn’t understand me, and I couldn’t understand them either," Ca Di says with a laugh. Some parents began to question the young teacher’s ability. Undeterred, she regularly talked with local residents to learn the area’s pronunciation and vocabulary. Only three schools in the province offer Khmer language classes, limiting opportunities for teachers to exchange experiences. At Hoa Dong Primary School, classes include both Kinh and Khmer students, so Khmer lessons are scheduled at the end of the school day. After regular classes, just over 10 students stay behind to study their mother tongue. Teaching Khmer is not easy, Ca Di says. The Khmer script has 68 vowels and consonants, nearly three times as many as Vietnamese. Students need about a year and a half just to master the alphabet, followed by more time to learn how to form syllables. Becoming proficient in reading and writing usually takes about three years. "Sometimes after finishing a new lesson, the students have already forgotten the previous one, so we have to start over. Without patience it’s easy to give up," she says. Khe Thi Sieng, now in 11th grade, still remembers her first days learning her mother tongue with Ca Di. Her parents worked as hired laborers and could not help with schoolwork, leaving Sieng self-conscious as she started from zero. Ca Di used digital lesson plans, projected images and videos about Khmer culture to make the lessons easier. She also recorded difficult words in Vietnamese to help students remember them. After nearly five years of steady effort, Sieng became fluent and one of Ca Di’s top students. Around that time, Oc Xa Quan, a school security guard who lived nearby and was 13 years older than Ca Di, was still single. After colleagues introduced them, the two began getting to know each other. "He’s the youngest of nine siblings, kind, hardworking and caring, so I felt drawn to him after a few meetings," she recalls. They married after two years and now have two sons. Besides their salaries as a teacher and school security guard, the couple farms one hectare of rice and cassava that their parents gave them. The rice mainly meets their household needs, while cassava brings in about VND20 million (US$767) per harvest in good years. Dang Cong Xuan, principal of Hoa Dong Primary School, describes Ca Di as a dedicated professional who has repeatedly completed outstanding work and received a certificate of merit from the provincial People’s Committee. She has also been recognized as a local emulation fighter and excellent teacher. "Ms. Ca Di often takes the initiative to use technology in her teaching and inspires students to love their ethnic language and script," Xuan says. According to the Tay Ninh Department of Education and Training, three primary schools in Phuoc Vinh, Tan Phu and Binh Minh wards currently offer Khmer classes to a total of 266 students. The classes are taught by only three teachers. "Every child who learns to read and write Khmer helps preserve a piece of ethnic culture for the next generation," Ca Di says.

picked.t: 베트남 최대 가전유통社 디엔마이산, 캄보디아 공식 철수…해외시장 인니가 유일
picked.body: 베트남 전자제품 체인 모바일월드의 인도네시아 체인 에라블루. (사진=모바일월드) 베트남 최대 가전제품 유통사 모바일월드(MWG)가 가전 소매 자회사 디엔마이산(DMX)의 캄보디아 사업을 완전히 정리하면서 해외 시장은 인도네시아 1곳만 남게 됐다. 베트남 재무부 산하 외국인투자청(FIA)은 지난달 17일부로 디엔마이산의 해외투자등록증 효력을 종료하는 결정을 내렸다. 지난 2017년 1월 최초 발급된 이 해외투자등록증은 모바일월드의 캄보디아 가전유통 체인 투자를 대상으로 한 것이었다. 당국은 디엔마이산이 지난 2월 제출한 신청서를 근거로 이번 종료 결정을 내렸다. 디엔마이산 측에 따르면 이번 결정은 해외투자사업 종료를 위한 법적 절차가 마무리됐음을 의미한다. 실제로는 캄보디아 사업부가 이미 지난해 1월 영업을 중단하고 청산 절차까지 완료한 상태로, 이번 결정이 회사의 현재 사업활동에 영향을 미치지는 않는다. 이번 결정에 따라 회사는 캄보디아에 남아 있는 자본·자산 전액을 베트남으로 회수하게 된다. 캄보디아는 디엔마이산의 첫 해외 시장이다. 동사는 지난 2017년 6월 캄보디아 수도 프놈펜에 첫 휴대폰 매장 ‘빅폰(BigPhone)’을 출점한 뒤, 2019년 체인명을 ‘블루트로닉스(Bluetronics)'로 변경하고 취급 품목을 가전제품 전반으로 넓혔다. 블루트로닉스는 2021년 중반 매장 55개로 정점을 찍었으나, 이후 사세 확장에 어려움을 겪었다. 2023년 2월 기준 프놈펜 매장 수는 단 2곳으로 줄었고, 그마저도 그해 1분기 모두 문을 닫았다. 당시 디엔마이산 관계자는 "6년간 운영한 끝에 캄보디아 사업을 중단하고 다른 사업모델에 집중하기로 했다"며 “캄보디아 시장 규모가 너무 작은 데다, 복잡한 세제 탓에 블루트로닉스가 현지 유통 업체들과 가격 경쟁력에서 밀렸다”고 철수 배경을 밝힌 바 있다. 한편, 인도네시아에서 합작 형태로 운영 중인 가전제품 체인 에라블루(Erablue)는 꾸준히 매장 수가 늘고 있다. 모바일월드에 따르면, 7월 말 기준 에라블루 매장 수는 283곳으로 전년 동기 대비 157곳 순증했다. 같은 기간 매출은 누적 2조2,000억 루피아(1억2,470만여 달러)로 89% 급증했다. 모바일월드는 에라블루 매장 수를 내년까지 500곳, 2030년까지 1,000곳으로 확대한다는 계획이다.
